\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\caption{Secondary validation on MovieLens 1M using seed 42. The tuned coupled NMF model is selected from the reduced validation grid, whereas the remaining baselines are evaluated using the same split.}
\label{tab:ml1m_secondary_validation_seed42}
\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcccccccc}
\toprule

\midrule
Biased MF & 0.8481 & 0.6673 & 0.0496 & 0.0301 & 0.0534 & 0.0444 & 0.0525 & 0.0569 \\
Plain NMF & 0.8498 & 0.6696 & 0.0533 & 0.0304 & 0.0591 & 0.0473 & 0.0551 & 0.0620 \\
Coupled NMF & 0.8717 & 0.6890 & 0.0386 & 0.0211 & 0.0390 & 0.0338 & 0.0362 & 0.0406 \\
Tuned Coupled NMF & 0.8594 & 0.6770 & 0.0545 & 0.0302 & 0.0591 & 0.0459 & 0.0506 & 0.0594 \\
Item-CF & 0.9986 & 0.7947 & 0.0028 & 0.0013 & 0.0027 & 0.0039 & 0.0035 & 0.0039 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
}
\vspace{0.35em}
\begin{minipage}{0.96\textwidth}
\footnotesize MovieLens 1M is used as a larger secondary validation dataset with genre-only item descriptors. The tuned coupled NMF improves substantially over the untuned coupled NMF and remains competitive with plain NMF on short-list ranking metrics, although plain NMF remains stronger on RMSE, MAE, and NDCG@10.
\end{minipage}
\end{table}

\begin{table}[htbp]

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
}
\vspace{0.35em}
\begin{minipage}{0.96\textwidth}
\footnotesize Positive relative improvement means that the tuned model improves over the untuned coupled NMF. For RMSE and MAE, lower values are better; for ranking metrics, higher values are better.
\end{minipage}
\end{table}
